name: Adin
overview: The name Adin appears in Scripture as the head of a Jewish family during the post-exilic period, specifically identified as a captive who returned to Jerusalem. The descendants of Adin are enumerated in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah, with the population of his children recorded as 454 in Ezra 2:15 and 655 in Nehemiah 7:20, indicating growth and continuity of this family line among the returned exiles. Additionally, Ezra 8:6 highlights a specific individual, Ebed, son of Jonathan from the sons of Adin, who returned with fifty males, emphasizing the faithful restoration of God's people after captivity.
